[PATH:empirical] Single-cell multi-omics analysis of CRISPR-edited human embryos, comparing off-target mutation profiles with chromatin accessibility and histone modification maps (e.g., ATAC-seq, ChIP-seq for H3K27ac) to quantify enrichment in regulatory regions and measure downstream gene expression changes. — Directly tests whether off-target mutations preferentially occur in non-coding regulatory regions and whether they alter gene expression in a therapeutically neutral manner, using high-resolution molecular profiling.

[PATH:theoretical] Mathematical modeling of off-target mutation distribution based on sequence homology and chromatin state, calibrated against published in vitro and in vivo editing data from high-fidelity editors (e.g., eSpCas9, Cas12a variants) in human cell lines or organoids. — Predicts expected enrichment patterns under neutral and non-neutral scenarios, providing a framework to compare against empirical data and assess statistical significance of any observed regulatory region bias.

[PATH:literature] Comparative meta-analysis of published preclinical studies (2019–2025) on germline editing in human embryos, focusing on off-target mutation rates reported for different editing platforms (e.g., CRISPR-Cas9, base editors, prime editors) and their correlation with editing efficiency — Synthesizing existing data across studies can reveal whether current evidence consistently supports high precision with negligible off-target mutations or whether variability and methodological limitations undermine that conclusion.
